title: Radiation: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation — questions and answers
claims: UVA accounts for approximately 95% of the UV radiation reaching the Earth's surface, penetrates deeper into the skin and is responsible for immediate tanning; recent studies suggest it may also enhance skin cancer development.
UVB is biologically active but cannot penetrate beyond superficial skin layers; it causes delayed tanning and burning and significantly promotes skin cancer development.
In mid-latitudes, UV levels are highest during the summer months in the four-hour period around solar noon.
UV levels increase by approximately 10% for every 1,000 m of altitude.
Grass, soil and water reflect less than 10% of incident UV; sand reflects about 15%, sea foam about 25%, and fresh snow almost doubles a person's UV exposure and can reflect as much as 80%.
Light or thin clouds have little effect on UV and may even enhance UV levels through scattering; an overcast day or cool breeze does not mean UV is low.
Most evidence suggests that altered behaviour and more outdoor activity, rather than ozone depletion, are the major cause of rising skin cancer rates.
